questions.q: Which city stands at the northern end of the Willamette Valley, where the Willamette River meets the Columbia?
questions.exp: The Willamette Valley runs about 240 kilometres (150 miles) south from Portland towards Eugene, between the Coast Range and the Cascades, with most of its vines in the hills of Yamhill County south-west of the city. The Columbia Valley lies far to the east of Seattle, beyond the Cascades, in Washington's rain shadow.

questions.q: Which climate category does the Court give the Columbia Valley?
questions.exp: The Cascades wring the Pacific rain out before it reaches the Columbia basin, which sees about 150 to 200 millimetres (six to eight inches) a year: a warm desert of long, hot, dry summers and cool nights, so every vine is irrigated. The Court calls the Willamette Valley, west of the mountains, cool Mediterranean with maritime influence.

questions.q: Beside Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, which third red does the Court list for the Columbia Valley?
questions.exp: The Court's Columbia Valley list runs Chardonnay, Riesling, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah, and the warm, dry desert east of the Cascades ripens Syrah to dark fruit and smoke, with the Walla Walla Valley and the Yakima Valley among its homes. Pinot Noir is the Willamette Valley's red, west of the Cascades in Oregon; Zinfandel and Malbec grow in Washington but are not on the Court's list.

questions.q: Which style does the Court list for Oregon but leave off its list for Washington?
questions.exp: Oregon makes traditional method sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and some Meunier, a style Argyle established in Dundee from 1987, beside its dry whites and dry reds; the Court lists Washington for dry whites and dry reds alone. Willamette Brut is aged for years on its lees, apple and brioche with fine bubbles.

questions.q: By the Court's account, what has kept phylloxera out of most of the Columbia Valley's vineyards?
questions.exp: Phylloxera struggles in the deep, sandy, free draining soils the Missoula Floods left on the desert floor, with cold winters and isolation adding to the barrier, so most Washington vines stand on their own roots and can be regrown from the base after a killing freeze. It is rare rather than absent: the pest was confirmed in some Walla Walla vineyards in 2019, and new plantings are more often grafted.

questions.q: Besides the Columbia Valley and the Walla Walla Valley, which AVA does the Court list as shared by Washington and Oregon?
questions.exp: The Columbia Gorge AVA straddles the river where it cuts through the Cascades, changing from wet in the west to dry in the east over a short stretch of river, and it is a separate AVA, not part of the Columbia Valley. Yakima Valley and Puget Sound lie wholly in Washington, and the Lewis-Clark Valley is shared with Idaho.

questions.q: The Court names three rivers as the Columbia Valley's water source: the Columbia, the Yakima and which other?
questions.exp: The Columbia and its tributaries, the Yakima and the Snake, feed the canals and drip lines without which nothing would grow in a basin of 150 to 200 millimetres (six to eight inches) of rain. The same Court cell adds the Van Duzer Corridor, which cools Oregon's Eola-Amity Hills, and the generally south-facing slopes of the Columbia Valley.

questions.q: Which of these producers named by the Court makes its wine in Washington's Walla Walla Valley?
questions.exp: Leonetti Cellar, founded in 1977, was Walla Walla's first modern winery, and its Cabernet and Merlot made the valley a prestige address. Domaine Serene, Erath and Ponzi are the Court's Willamette names, with Eyrie and Domaine Drouhin; Quilceda Creek, L'Ecole No. 41 and Chateau Ste. Michelle complete its Washington list.

questions.q: Besides salmon, which vegetable does the Court pair with Willamette Valley Pinot Noir?
questions.exp: The earthy sweetness of roast butternut squash meets the red fruit and forest floor of Willamette Pinot Noir, and salmon's richness suits its silky tannin and fresh acid. For the firmer tannin of Washington Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot the Court's pairing is beef or lamb.
